morphology_keys.lookalike_separators: ARUNDO vs PHRAGMITES: Both make tall jointed riparian canes and feathery heads. Arundo usually has broad clasping leaf bases, a robust cane and a more upright branching panicle; common reed often has a more drooping plume. A definitive flowering check is WHERE HAIRS GROW: Arundo has a glabrous RACHILLA (axis between florets) but silky hairs on the basal lemma/callus; Phragmites has LONG SILKY RACHILLA HAIRS and usually glabrous lemmas. Their ligules can BOTH be fringed — a 'hairless Arundo ligule' is NOT a dependable rule. Do not call a Phragmites stand introduced/invasive without independent lineage evidence.

field_id_lesson.look_here_first: GIANT REED: begin with robust jointed canes and broad clasping leaves; inspect the actual leaf collar and mature flowering plume in the licensed macro panels. For look-alike Phragmites, confirm glabrous Arundo spikelet RACHILLA versus long silky Phragmites rachilla hairs on a magnified ripe spikelet; the Arundo ligule itself CAN have a ciliate fringe. No removal or exact Phragmites lineage ID from plume size alone.
crew_checkpoints: FIRST: view archived whole stand—dense robust cane-like culms and broad drooping leaves suggest giant reed but do not identify it alone.

SECOND: use the photographed true blade/sheath junction. A pale rounded clasping base and ciliate membranous ligule are visible. Both Arundo and Phragmites can have a fringed ligule; hair presence at collar is NOT a safe binary split.
THIRD: see the branching terminal Arundo flowering plume in the new source photo; it tends more upright, but panicle shape varies and is not conclusive.

FOURTH (DECISIVE WITH A MICROSCOPE): remove one ripe spikelet with permission, open it over a millimeter scale. Arundo: rachilla itself hairless; white hairs on lower lemma/callus. Phragmites: long silky hairs ON the rachilla between florets, typically glabrous lemma.

FIFTH: do NOT confuse species ID with nativity. Arundo donax is introduced in Texas; Phragmites australis includes native North American, introduced Eurasian and southern Gulf Coast lineages. Resolve any Phragmites lineage separately before treatment.

look_alikes.check: Use mature SAME-SPECIMEN spikelets: Phragmites rachilla with long silky hairs versus Arundo rachilla glabrous, hairs chiefly on Arundo lemma/callus. Both can have ciliate ligules. Native lineage/introduced provenance remains a separate management decision.

Native giant cutgrass can form tall waterside stands; compare its more open grass panicle, extremely rough cutting leaf margins, and very different floret/spikelet arrangement. Do not classify from height or proximity to water alone.
Tall introduced Johnsongrass with characteristic conspicuously paired spikelets on an open branched panicle rather than the true Arundo floret group; generally narrower leaves and smaller canes.

diagnostic_species_finalization_20261023.look_here_first: GIANT REED: follow one robust 2–6 m jointed cane to broad leaves with rounded clasping blade-base lobes and a dense 30–60 cm plume. At the true collar find a short CILIATE MEMBRANOUS ligule. Do not separate from Phragmites by plume size or ligule hairs alone: inspect a ripe floret for where the silky hairs originate.

measurable_field_key.growth_form: Robust rhizomatous perennial, erect cane-like culms commonly 2–6 m; thick knotty woody rhizomes and many jointed culms, not an annual tuft. Leaf blades commonly 30–60 cm by 2.5–5 cm, rounded to clasping at base.
measurable_field_key.ligule_collar: Short membranous ligule with ciliate fringe, reported 0.7–2 mm in regional floras; rounded/ear-like clasping blade-base lobes; do not mistake adjacent sheath-mouth hairs for the membrane. Measure a true opened blade–sheath junction with 1-mm scale.
measurable_field_key.panicle: Large, profusely branched, often upright oblong plume, commonly 30–60 cm long; shape is supportive, not diagnostic against common reed.
measurable_field_key.spikelet: Pedicelled laterally compressed spikelets approximately 8–15 mm, commonly 3–5 florets; florets disarticulate above persistent glumes. Do not call a whole spikelet one seed.
measurable_field_key.glumes: Two persistent, roughly equal narrow membranous glumes, often 8.5–13 mm, each typically 3–5-veined, mostly glabrous and without long awns. Published ranges vary; use attached mature material and a millimeter rule.
measurable_field_key.lemma_palea: Fertile lemma generally 6–12 mm, 3–9-veined depending regional treatment, conspicuously silky-hairy on its lower back/callus with hairs often 5–8 mm. Palea shorter, usually about half to two-thirds lemma length, two-veined and ciliate on keels.
measurable_field_key.awn: Glumes essentially awnless. Fertile lemma apex may be minutely two-toothed and bear a SHORT median awn/awnlet, approximately 1–3 mm, arising near/between apical teeth; do not mislabel the long silky lemma hairs as awns.
measurable_field_key.decisive_hair_placement: Between successive florets, the Arundo rachilla internodes are glabrous or lack the conspicuous long silky rachilla hairs of Phragmites; Arundo silk is chiefly on lemma backs and floret bases. A basal tuft near the lowest floret may occur, so never oversimplify to 'every part of rachilla hairless'.

diagnostic_species_finalization_20261023.local_lookalikes: Phragmites australis: rhizomatous wetland reed with long silky hairs along the rachilla between florets and usually glabrous lemmas; native, introduced and Gulf Coast lineages require independent evidence. Zizaniopsis miliacea: native giant cutgrass, extremely rough cutting leaf margins and different male/female floral organization; do not decide from stand height. Sorghum halepense: tall rhizomatous Johnsongrass with paired sessile/pedicellate spikelets in an open panicle rather than Arundo's multi-flowered spikelets.
last_mile_photo_arrow_gaps: SAME TEXAS PLANT: rooted or previously disturbed rhizome, intact jointed culm node, broad clasping leaf base and complete plume with centimeter ruler; no new excavation solely for a photograph.
TRUE COLLAR 10–20×: opened blade–sheath junction with short fringed membrane and clasping lobes, measured against 1-mm scale; compare Phragmites collar at matching scale.
MATURE SPIKELET 10–20×: intact 8–15 mm spikelet, two detached glumes with veins, and individual fertile lemma/palea; each with 1-mm ruler and independent specimen determination.

DECISIVE DISSECTION: same specimen Arundo rachilla internodes versus basal lemma/callus hairs, paired with verified Phragmites rachilla hairs at same magnification. Arrow only anatomically visible structures.
AWN DETAIL: isolated fertile lemma apex with short 1–3 mm median awnlet, distinguish from 5–8 mm basal silk and glume tips; photo-rights and attribution verified individually.
